_meta.source: Every point resolved individually against OpenStreetMap on 30–31 July 2026 — by Nominatim search for the named sites, and by an Overpass named-feature sweep of the Ver-o-Peso complex and the Icoaraci waterfront. None is estimated. The port pin is the tender landing at Icoaraci, 18–20 km north of everything else on the map, which is the single most important thing this map has to show. The anchorage position itself in Guajará Bay is not published in any source I could reach and is deliberately not marked.

port_pin.label: Terminal Hidroviário e Turístico de Icoaraci — the tender landing

bbox_hint.note: Belém stands on the right bank of the Baía do Guajará, on the Rio Pará estuary — the southern arm of the Amazon delta, separated from the main stem by Marajó Island. The tender lands at Icoaraci in the north; the historic centre is 18–20 km south.

fit.why: Auto-fit spans the 18 km from the Icoaraci tender landing to a historic centre 2 km across, and collapses every downtown marker into one clump — measured at 5-11 px between neighbours in a 678x500 container, against a 36 px marker. The map therefore opens on the walkable centre, where seven of the ten points are. The rule is consistent and stated in the intro: the two boat-distance points, Icoaraci to the north and Ilha do Combu to the south, are one zoom-out away. Nothing is removed from the map.

pois.name: Complexo do Ver-o-Peso
pois.notes: The weighing station dates from 1625; the twelve-sided iron fish market from 1901, prefabricated in England and New York. IPHAN-listed 9 November 1977. Around it: the 1867 Mercado de Carnes Francisco Bolonha, the Solar da Beira, the Doca, and the Feira do Açaí behind the fort. Rebuilt in stages through 2025 and January 2026. About 1,193 licensed traders.

pois.name: Forte do Presépio (Forte do Castelo)
pois.notes: The 1616 foundation point of Belém, on the bluff above the açaí fair, with an archaeology museum. Five minutes' walk from Ver-o-Peso. The Casa das Onze Janelas — an 18th-century house, now a contemporary art museum with the best bay view in the old city — is immediately alongside, as is the Catedral da Sé.

pois.name: Estação das Docas
pois.notes: Three converted riverfront warehouses of the old port plus a passenger terminal, opened 13 May 2000 — 32,000 m² along 500 m of frontage. Air-conditioned, level and safe; the sensible lunch and the indoor fallback for the afternoon downpour. Not where the ship docks, whatever older guides imply.

pois.name: Theatro da Paz
pois.notes: Opened 15 February 1878, eighteen years before the Teatro Amazonas. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List 27 July 2026 as one of two components of Amazonia Theatres, criteria (ii)(iv) — together with Praça da República, which it stands in and which is inside the inscription. Hourly 45-minute tours, R$10, 40-person cap, closed Mondays.

pois.name: Basílica de Nossa Senhora de Nazaré
pois.notes: Built 1909 on the model of St Paul Outside the Walls in Rome — marble, mosaic, and the shrine of Our Lady of Nazareth. About 3 km from the Cidade Velha, a taxi ride rather than a walk. The Círio de Nazaré procession each October is the largest Marian procession in the world; it falls nowhere near a world-cruise call.

pois.name: Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi
pois.notes: Founded 1866, one of the oldest scientific institutions in the Amazon. The visitable Parque Zoobotânico is a compact urban rainforest with manatees, harpy eagles and jaguars. Open Wednesday to Sunday 09:00–16:00, R$3 — closed Monday and Tuesday, which is a real constraint on a fixed port date.

pois.name: Mangal das Garças
pois.notes: A landscaped riverside park at the edge of the Cidade Velha — butterfly house, aviary, an aquatic-life exhibit and a lighthouse-style tower over the Guamá. Close enough to combine with the fort and the Feliz Lusitânia complex. It was on the official welcome tours given to the January 2026 cruise arrivals.

pois.name: Trapiche do Outeiro
pois.notes: The waterfront of the Outeiro district, immediately north of Icoaraci and linked to it by a cable-stayed bridge opened 18 October 2025. This is where the Terminal Portuário de Outeiro was rebuilt for COP30 with a pier of roughly 710 m at a cost of over R$233 million, expressly to berth two large ships. It is complete and operational — and cruise ships are still not using it, because low tide at typical cruise arrival and departure times makes the manoeuvre difficult. The single thing most likely to change this port by 2028.

pois.name: Ilha de Cotijuba
pois.notes: A river island served by the same Icoaraci terminal the tender lands at — around 27,000 passengers a month on the local route, and home to more than 10,000 islanders. Not a realistic port-day trip on top of the city transfer, but it explains what the terminal was actually built for.

pois.name: Ilha do Combu
pois.notes: An environmental protection area in the Rio Guamá directly opposite the city — 10 to 15 minutes by boat from the Terminal Hidroviário Ruy Barata, and less than a kilometre off the shoreline. Dense várzea forest, igarapés, ribeirinho households living from açaí and cacao, and a bean-to-bar chocolate maker on the island. The best answer to "can I see the rainforest on a port day."
